newsitem.title: UK: World oil prices see late recovery.
newsitem.headline: World oil prices see late recovery.

text.p: World oil prices recovered in late trade on Monday after traders had pushed prices to new lows earlier in the day.

April West Texas Intermediate crude on the New York Mercantile Exchange fell to an eight-month low as it dipped briefly below $20 a barrel in the afternoon. The contract recovered by the close, ending the day just a few cents down at $20.26 a barrel.

But traders warned that an end to the winter heating oil season had yet to give way to strong gasoline demand ahead of the driving season, which could prevent any further price gains and overshadow signs of tighter North Sea crude oil supplies.

At 2034 GMT, bellweather North Sea Brent crude futures for April delivery had ended the days trading on the IPE futures seven cents higher at $18.92 a barrel, having recovered from the day's low of $18.68 a barrel.
"Overall both European and U.S. fundamentals are still fairly weak," said Leslie Nicholas, energy analyst at GNI Ltd in London.
"There's just too much crude around and (refining) margins are awful. Why should prices go up?" a trader of North Sea crudes said.
Norwegian oil giant Statoil said on Monday that all operations at the offshore Statfjord and Gullfaks fields were returning to normal following production and loading disruptions due to bad weather.

A trader was also believed to have fixed two large vessels of Brent crude oil totalling at least 5.5 million barrels to be shipped to the United States and South Africa. The market had been sceptical that so much crude oil would leave the Northwest Europe market.

"The cooler weather coming into the States might take some of the immediate onus off heating oil...but for the deep-seeded shorts, there is no great rationale to cover (their positions) yet," a commission house energy analyst said.
Futures prices of gas oil, or home heating oil, which fell 22 percent in the month of February to an eight-month low on Friday, had lost a further $2.25 to $160.25 a tonne by close of play on Monday.

Private forecaster Weather Services Corp predicted temperatures in the Northeast United States would drop to below normal early this week before warming up near mid-week and reaching above normal levels in the next week to 10 days.

The warmer weather has exacerbated the sharp selloff in the last few weeks that came on the back of rising production from the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) and countries outside the oil group.
The price of OPEC's basket of crudes fell to $19.19 a barrel last week, down sharply from $20.22 the previous week and the $23.19 average in January.

U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan said over the weekend that he was unaware of any Iraqi talks aimed at enabling Baghdad to increase its income from its oil-for-food deal with the United Nations, as Iraq had indicated last week.

The deal, which permits Iraq to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months to buy needed supplies for its people, has contributed to rising OPEC production and the downward pressure on prices, traders said.
